title: Shah Rukh Khan Set for Cameo in Allu Arjun's Rs 1,000 Crore Epic 'Raaka'
excerpt: Reports indicate SRK will film a pivotal appearance in director Atlee's ambitious two-part sci-fi spectacle, reuniting with his Jawan collaborator while Allu Arjun takes on triple roles.
body:
• Shah Rukh Khan has reportedly agreed to a cameo in Allu Arjun's upcoming film Raaka, directed by Atlee (Jawan), according to India Today and multiple industry sources.
  • Raaka is being planned as a two-part film spanning two timelines — a tribal Puranic-Vedic era and a contemporary setting — with a reported budget exceeding Rs 1,000 crore.
  • Deepika Padukone is confirmed as the female lead, with reports also naming Mrunal Thakur, Janhvi Kapoor, and Rashmika Mandanna in the ensemble cast.
  • The cameo marks the first on-screen collaboration between Shah Rukh Khan and Allu Arjun, after a planned cameo in Jawan fell through due to Pushpa 2 scheduling conflicts.

Shah Rukh Khan is set to appear in a cameo role in Raaka, the high-budget sci-fi spectacle starring Allu Arjun and directed by Atlee, according to an India Today report corroborated by multiple industry publications. The appearance would mark the first time Khan and Allu Arjun share the screen.

The film, produced by Sun Pictures, is mounted on a budget reportedly exceeding Rs 1,000 crore, positioning it among the costliest Indian films ever made. Khan's cameo is expected to be filmed overseas, though the specific timeline has not been disclosed.

Two Parts, Two Timelines

According to India Today, Raaka is being developed as a two-part release. The narrative will span two distinct worlds — one rooted in a tribal, Puranic-Vedic era and the other set in a contemporary urban landscape.

Deepika Padukone is the only cast member officially confirmed by the makers alongside Allu Arjun. However, reports indicate that Mrunal Thakur will play the female lead in the modern timeline, while Padukone, Janhvi Kapoor, and Rashmika Mandanna are expected to feature in the historical portion.

Allu Arjun is reportedly playing three distinct roles in the film — a cop, a father figure, and a hybrid half-human, half-beast character. The first-look poster, released on his 44th birthday on April 8, showed the actor in a rugged, werewolf-inspired avatar with sharp claws and a feral aesthetic.

The Jawan Connection

Khan's involvement stems from his close working relationship with director Atlee, who helmed the 2023 blockbuster Jawan. That film grossed over Rs 1,100 crore worldwide and cemented the Chennai-based director as one of Indian cinema's most bankable filmmakers.

"Happy Birthday @alluarjun … the poster is intriguing and amazing just like you are. Can't wait to see what you guys have put together. This experience will be… in Atlee's words — Mass masss massss!!"

— Shah Rukh Khan, on X (formerly Twitter)

Industry sources told Filmfare that Khan agreed to the role immediately, motivated by his bond with both Atlee and Allu Arjun. The cameo has been described as a pivotal "catalyst" role in the second half, linked to the film's sci-fi and fantasy elements.

The collaboration carries symbolic weight. Allu Arjun was originally slated for a cameo in Jawan in 2023 but had to withdraw due to scheduling conflicts with Pushpa 2: The Rule. Khan stepping into Raaka is widely seen as completing that unfulfilled crossover.

Cross-Industry Convergence

Raaka exemplifies the ongoing merger between Bollywood and South Indian cinema that has accelerated since the pan-Indian success of films like Baahubali, RRR, and Pushpa. Directors like Atlee, S.S. Rajamouli, and Lokesh Kanagaraj are now building multi-regional casts as standard practice.

For overseas audiences, this convergence simplifies what was once a fragmented market. Diaspora viewers who grew up on Shah Rukh Khan's Bollywood romances now follow Telugu and Tamil cinema with equal enthusiasm — and Raaka targets both demographics simultaneously.

The film's technical team includes music composer Sai Abhyankkar for songs and background score. International VFX studios are reportedly involved in the production, with extensive CGI planned for the creature designs and dual-timeline sequences.

What's Next

No official release date has been announced for either part of Raaka. Filming is currently underway in Mumbai, and Allu Arjun is simultaneously developing another project with director Lokesh Kanagaraj, tentatively titled AA23.

Sun Pictures, the Chennai-based production house behind the Master and Sarkar franchises, has not officially responded to reports about the two-part structure or Khan's cameo. An official cast announcement is expected in the coming months.
